sn55.27:2.2: “Sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is sick, suffering, gravely ill.
sn55.27:2.3: He bows with your head to your feet.
sn55.27:2.5: ‘Sir, please visit him at his home out of sympathy.’”
sn55.27:5.2: Seeing in themselves that distrust of the teaching, they’re frightened and terrified, and fear what awaits them after death.
sn55.27:6.2: Seeing in themselves that distrust of the Saṅgha, they’re frightened and terrified, and fear what awaits them after death.
sn55.27:8.4: That Blessed One is … teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.
sn55.27:9.2: The teaching is well proclaimed by the Blessed One … to be realized directly by the wise.
sn55.27:9.3: Seeing in themselves that experiential confidence in the teaching, they’re not frightened or terrified, and don’t fear what awaits them after death.
sn55.27:10.2: The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing well … the supreme field of merit for the world.
